#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -N 1
#flux: --ntasks-per-node=1
#flux: --cpus-per-task=1
#flux: -t 12:00:00
#flux: --job-name=2Lsim

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU and will NOT be allocated 40GB of memory.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
# #SBATCH --mem=40GB

module purge

# The NUM_JULIA_THREADS variable is set to the number of CPUs requested for the task.
# This is necessary as Flux does not provide a standard equivalent to nproc within the allocation.
export NUM_JULIA_THREADS=1

# $FLUX_JOB_ID is the equivalent of $SLURM_JOB_ID
rundir=$SCRATCH/twolayer_simulation/$FLUX_JOB_ID
mkdir -p $rundir

# It is assumed driver.sbatch is the name of the original submission script.
# The path will depend on where the job is submitted from.
cp TwoLayerSimulation.jl Driver.jl driver.sbatch $rundir
cp Parameters.jl $rundir/Parameters.jl
cd $rundir

# Flux does not provide a standard equivalent to $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK.
# The value is hardcoded to match the number of CPUs requested by the '--cpus-per-task' directive.
julia -t 1 Driver.jl > run.log

exit

reasons: Validation failed at directives: --ntasks-per-node=1, --cpus-per-task=1. The standard short-form options ('-n', '-c') are more portable and widely supported.
issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, two essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) and the request for 40GB of memory (`--mem=40GB`). While the translated script is syntactically valid (aside from the reasons noted above), it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU and will receive a default, likely insufficient, memory allocation. Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.

The original script set `NUM_JULIA_THREADS` to `nproc`, which would use all cores on the node. The translated script hardcodes this to `1`, which is a significant change in behavior and will prevent the Julia application from taking advantage of a multi-core environment.
The script relies on an environment variable `$SCRATCH` that is not defined within the script. This must be present in the submission environment for the job to succeed.

The script copies `driver.sbatch` into the run directory. This suggests the user might intend to chain jobs, but there is no `sbatch` or `flux batch` command to do so. This file copy might be unnecessary.

#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

# Corrected based on validation feedback, using standard short-form options.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: -t 12:00:00
#flux: --job-name=2Lsim

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU and will NOT be allocated 40GB of memory.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
# #SBATCH --mem=40GB

module purge

# The original script set NUM_JULIA_THREADS to `nproc` (all cores on the node).
# The resource request is only for 1 CPU, which is a contradiction.
# We will hardcode the thread count to match the requested CPUs for consistency.
export NUM_JULIA_THREADS=1

# $FLUX_JOB_ID is the equivalent of $SLURM_JOB_ID
rundir=$SCRATCH/twolayer_simulation/$FLUX_JOB_ID
mkdir -p $rundir

# It is assumed driver.sbatch is the name of the original submission script.
# The path will depend on where the job is submitted from.
cp TwoLayerSimulation.jl Driver.jl driver.sbatch $rundir
cp Parameters.jl $rundir/Parameters.jl
cd $rundir

# The number of threads for the Julia application is hardcoded to match the requested CPUs.
julia -t 1 Driver.jl > run.log

exit

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, two essential resource requests from the original Slurm script were omitted: the request for a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) and the request for 40GB of memory (`--mem=40GB`). While the translated script is syntactically valid, it is functionally incorrect. It will not be allocated a GPU and will receive a default, likely insufficient, memory allocation. Both omissions will almost certainly cause the job to fail at runtime.

The original script set `NUM_JULIA_THREADS` to `nproc`, which would use all available cores on the node. The translated script hardcodes this to `1` to match the `-c 1` request. This is a significant change in behavior and will prevent the Julia application from taking advantage of a multi-core environment, even if more cores were requested.
The script relies on an environment variable `$SCRATCH` that is not defined within the script. This must be present in the submission environment for the job to succeed.

The script copies `driver.sbatch` into the run directory. This suggests the user might intend to chain jobs, but there is no `sbatch` or `flux batch` command to do so. This file copy might be unnecessary.

#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --mem=40GB
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=2Lsim

module purge

export NUM_JULIA_THREADS=`nproc`

rundir=$SCRATCH/twolayer_simulation/$SLURM_JOB_ID
mkdir -p $rundir
cp TwoLayerSimulation.jl Driver.jl driver.sbatch $rundir
cp Parameters.jl $rundir/Parameters.jl
cd $rundir

julia -t $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK Driver.jl > run.log

exit
